title: How Much Does a Closet Remodel Cost? [2026 Data]
summary: The cost of a closet remodel depends on the closet size, materials used, and the level of customization. Learn what else influences your closet remodel cost.

Cost Insights:


-


Professional closet remodeling costs range from **$500** to **$22,000** , with an average project around **$4,100** depending on your closet size and design.


-


Your closet type affects the total, with walk-in closets needing more materials and customization than reach-in or standalone designs.


-


Budget for demolition and prep work at around 10% of your project cost, plus permits for structural changes between $300 and $900.


-


[Hiring a local closet making professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/closet-makers/) ensures your remodel maximizes storage space and delivers a functional, organized result.


In 2026, the national average cost for a closet remodel is **$4,100** , with most homeowners spending between **$2,300** and **$6,700** . Your final cost will depend primarily on the closet’s size and type, the materials you choose, the extent of any structural changes, and the level of customization.


## Closet Remodel Cost by Size: What Homeowners Pay


Neil/ Adobe Stock Photography


Closet size affects remodeling costs, but the relationship is not linear—larger closets tend to include more luxurious features, like custom wooden molding or silent drawers, which drive prices up faster than square footage alone. Smaller closets often skip those extras simply because the space does not support them. What matters more than raw size is the style of the remodel and the accessories you choose. Here’s how closet remodeling costs are affected by the size of the closet in square feet:


Closet Size (Square Feet) Average Cost in 2026


10 $500–$1,900


20 $900–$2,800


40 $1,800–$4,500


80 $3,400–$8,000


100 $5,000–$12,000


150 $8,000–$21,000


The average non-walk-in closet is around 8 square feet, while a walk-in closet can range from 20 to over 150 square feet.


## General Contractor Cost: What to Budget For


[General contractors charge](https://www.angi.com/articles/general-contractor-pricing.htm) a per-project fee of **10% to 25%** of the total project cost. If you prefer to pay hourly, expect to pay **$120 to $500 or more per hour** , depending on crew size and project complexity. A general contractor brings the skills and connections needed for a closet remodel, including access to[local closet makers](https://www.angi.com/nearme/closet-makers/) who specialize in this work.

## Carpenter Costs: What Drives the Final Price?


Hourly[rates for carpenters](https://www.angi.com/articles/carpenter-cost.htm) range from **$40 to $150** , depending on the complexity of the work and the materials involved. Some wood species take significantly longer to shape, which can push labor costs toward the higher end of that range. Custom woodwork in a closet remodel should always be handled by a professional carpenter—there is no substitute for hands-on experience and mastery of the medium.


## Electrician Cost: What Do They Charge per Hour?


Hiring an[electrician costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-hire-electrician.htm) **$60 to $100 per hour** on average. Any electrical elements in your closet remodel should be handled by a licensed pro rather than attempted as a DIY task. Walk-in closets almost always require electrical work for overhead and recessed lighting, as well as light switches.


## Additional Pros to Consider Hiring: What They May Cost


Larger closet remodels with structural elements may require an architect, and an interior designer can help personalize the finished space. For projects that need both, budgeting for these additional pros upfront helps avoid surprises.


-


**Hiring an architect:** Homeowners can expect to pay around **$3,000** for an architect's time and expertise. Project fees often hover around **15%** of the total cost, and an[architect's hourly rate](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-architect-cost.htm) typically runs around **$125 per hour** .


-


**Hiring an interior designer:** Expect to spend **$5 to $15 per square foot** on the[cost of an interior designer](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-hire-interior-designer.htm) . Closets carry a premium per-square-foot rate because of their smaller size, though that rate drops as the project grows—a small walk-in closet typically costs between **$300 and $600** to design, while a larger walk-in can cost **over $2,000** .

## Closet Remodel Costs by Location: Where It Costs the Most


Your location affects closet remodel costs because labor and material prices vary by region. Homeowners in high-cost areas, including parts of New York and California, typically pay more than those in lower-cost regions. The closet’s location within your home also matters: Ground-floor projects may cost less than upper-floor remodels because materials and tools are easier to access, although the difference is typically no more than **10%** .

## Closet Remodel Cost Factors: What Affects the Price?


You have a few options when it comes to remodeling your closet, including its design and any special features. You should also factor in the cost of demolition work and permits, if you plan to remove walls.


### Type of Closet


Walk-in closets cost the most to remodel, while reach-in closets are the least expensive. Reach-in, standalone, and basic built-in closets generally have smaller footprints and fewer customization options, keeping material and labor costs lower. Walk-in closets require more flooring, shelving, and storage components and may include premium features such as custom lighting, islands, mirrors, seating, and vanities. Adding electrical wiring for lighting, outlets, or other features can increase the total cost by several hundred dollars.

### Accessories or Special Features


There are many features to consider when remodeling a closet, depending on its size and your desired aesthetic and functional outcomes. Unlike a kitchen, where certain items are required (stove, sink, etc.), a closet can be adorned as much or as little as you want. The table below breaks down common closet remodel accessories, as well as their average costs:


Feature Average Cost in 2026


Electronic clothing rack $450–$2,100


Island with drawers $900–$5,200


Recessed lighting $150–$600


Skylight $1,700–$2,500


Safe $400–$3,000


Chandelier $800–$9,100


Surround sound system $1,100–$4,000


### Demolition and Prep


Demolition typically accounts for around **10%** of the total closet remodeling cost, while prep costs vary based on the closet’s size, condition, and project complexity. A small closet may require only an hour of preparation, but a larger or more complex remodel can take several days and require specialized equipment or additional labor. Include both expenses in your budget before installation begins.


### Permits


A full closet remodel that involves layout changes or structural work will require a permit, which costs between **$300 and $900** . Most home improvement projects fall under this requirement, and closet remodels are no exception. The[penalties for building without a permit](https://www.angi.com/articles/common-problems-when-you-dont-pull-permit.htm) can be severe, including a requirement to undo the remodel entirely — so secure permits before any work begins.

## Why You Should Hire a Pro for a Closet Remodel


[Hiring a local closet remodel pro](https://www.angi.com/nearme/closet-makers/) costs more upfront, but you benefit from expert design, efficient use of space, and high-quality materials that transform your closet into a functional and organized space. Pros bring the right tools, experience, and craftsmanship to ensure your remodel is completed on time and without unexpected costs.


### Here’s why it’s ideal to hire a closet remodel pro


Remodeling a closet involves design planning, installation of shelves, rods, drawers, and possibly electrical work for lighting. Here are some of the top reasons to work with a pro:


-


Professionals have the expertise to design a closet that maximizes storage, organizes your items efficiently, and ensures everything is installed securely.


-


They can offer custom options, like built-in shelving, pull-out racks, or custom cabinetry, tailored to your space and personal preferences.


-


Hiring a pro ensures proper measurements and structural adjustments, so your remodel integrates seamlessly with the room's layout and doesn't cause any future issues.


-


Many pros also handle the finishing touches, including painting, lighting, or flooring, helping to complete the space to a high standard without additional contractors.


### If you want to DIY parts of the project


If you want to take on some tasks yourself, here are a few DIY steps that can help reduce time and labor costs:


-


Clear out the closet and remove any existing shelving or storage systems before the remodel begins to make the space easier to work in.


-


Plan your closet layout in advance, considering what types of clothing, accessories, or shoes you want to store, so the pro can design your storage system efficiently.


-


If you plan to add lighting or electrical components, ensure the area is prepped by adding outlets or clear access points before the professional begins their work.


## Closet Remodel vs. Renovate


xy/ Adobe Stock Photography


When you're determining what to do with your closet you need to decide whether you're going to renovate the space or go through[a full remodel](https://www.angi.com/articles/closet-remodel-everything-you-need-to-know.htm) . Most closet remodels make the space more functional and larger, while a renovation gives an aesthetic boost.


For most small closets that do not need to be expanded, a renovation makes more sense and saves a lot of money. A full remodel is best for larger projects or grander visions.


## Tips to Reduce Cost While Remodeling a Closet


There are many ways to save some cash during the remodel, including:


-


Using LED lighting instead of recessed.


-


Using dollar store storage bins. Paint them to match the walls.


-


Using recycled materials like piping for hanging rods.


-


Utilizing the back of the[closet door](https://www.angi.com/articles/cost-to-install-closet-door.htm) as shoe storage.


-


Installing mirrors to create the illusion of more space.


-


DIYing everything except structural alterations and electrical.


## Does a Closet Remodel Increase Home Value?


A closet remodel likely won't raise the price of the home directly but if you're a seller, buyers appreciate this detail. This means that you may not be able to raise the price of your home to the exact amount of the remodel cost, but it should entice more people to make offers. The return on investment (ROI) of a closet remodel is usually between **50%** **and** **60%** of the total project cost.


Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Closet Pro


-


Share the dimensions of the closet space and discuss your storage needs (e.g., hanging rods, shelves, drawers) to help the pro design the most functional layout.


-


Ask about materials and finishes for shelving, cabinetry, and flooring, and whether there are options that fit your budget and style preferences.


-


Discuss any prep work, like clearing out the closet or removing old shelving, so the pro can get started right away.


-


Confirm whether unexpected costs could arise from issues like uneven walls or ceiling height that may affect the design or installation.


-


If you're considering add-ons, such as lighting, mirrors, or built-in organizers, ask if it makes sense to include those in the initial design to save on labor costs.

Luxury closets will have even more items, like felt-lined drawers for watches and jewelry, in-wall safes, electronic shoe storage, or a tablet catalog of their items.


There are certainly luxury upgrades you can make but you can seriously improve the look and functionality of a closet without spending much money. Color matching will make the closet seem bigger so any shelves painted the same as the wall is a good tip. While pre-made closet organizers may seem expensive they offer an aesthetic look that's hard to achieve with DIY methods. Lastly, removing clutter and unworn items will help the closet seem bigger and cleaner.


You can turn an adjacent room into a walking closet by just rearranging the room. This means removing the furniture and adding racks and an island in the center if you have that in your budget. Houses with two bedrooms connected to each other are great options for large walk-in closets that don't require any structural changes or much building whatsoever.
